title: Tensor projection formula for derived open extension by zero
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme of universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme] and $U$ any open. Specify derived categories on $X$ and the over-site of $U$ with morphism universe $w$ [def-pc-derived-category], and use the standard derived category of $U.toScheme$ with morphism universe $u+1$. Let $R$ be the composite of derived over-site restriction and the derived over-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], using the recorded derived tensor structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For every strong monoidal structure $m$ on $R$, there is a left adjoint $J$ to $R$, with adjunction $a$, such that for every $A$ on $U.toScheme$ and $K$ on $X$, the adjunction transpose of $(a.unit_A \otimes 1_{RK});\mu_m(JA,K)$, namely a morphism $J(A\otimes RK)\to JA\otimes K$, is invertible. This statement contains no internal Hom or tensor-Hom equivalence.

proof.text: Exact extension by zero J is left adjoint to restriction, with invertible unit. Transport across overEquiv and derive the adjunction using exact functors. Localization factorization and the two adjunction identities construct the derived unit and counit independently of their universes. The ordinary stalks of J(A) vanish outside U and agree with A inside U; exactness gives the same statements on derived cohomology. Thus J is fully faithful and its essential image consists of complexes with cohomology stalks zero outside U.

For A on U, J(A) tensor K has vanishing cohomology stalks outside U: replace both inputs by K-flat complexes and compute tensor on stalks. The stalk of J(A) is acyclic outside U and tensor with the other K-flat stalk stays acyclic. Restriction reflects isomorphisms between supported complexes because a cone with zero restricted cohomology has zero cohomology at every remaining stalk as well.

Transpose (unit_A tensor identity);mu_m(J(A),K) to obtain J(A tensor R(K)) -> J(A) tensor K. Both objects are supported on U, and its restriction is a composite of the invertible unit and tensorator by the adjunction identities; hence it is invertible. This argument uses any natural invertible tensorator, not a distinguished choice of representatives.

Return the explicitly constructed derived extension-by-zero functor J, its derived adjunction with R, and invertibility of every projection mate. J is fixed up to the unique adjunction isomorphism; the construction works for zero inputs and the empty open.

theorem exists_openExtension_projectionFormula (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] :
    let E := (Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let R := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ E
    ∀ m : R.Monoidal,
      letI := m
      ∃ J : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme ⥤ schemeDerivedCategory X,
        ∃ adj : J ⊣ R,
          ∀ (A : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme) (K : schemeDerivedCategory X),
            IsIso ((adj.homEquiv (A ⊗ R.obj K) (J.obj A ⊗ K)).symm
              ((adj.unit.app A ⊗ₘ 𝟙 (R.obj K)) ≫
                (Functor.Monoidal.μIso R (J.obj A) K).hom))
